headline: Highest risk is data leakage from opik’s broad network egress into pathway’s document-processing context; other pairwise risks are limited by pathway’s no-write/no-network defaults.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Opik can emit REST API outputs and has broad network egress, so if its output is manually or programmatically fed into Pathway, prompt-like content could be misread. Pathway has no clipboard, MCP, stdin/stdout, or filesystem ingestion surfaces listed, so the bridge is not default. This is a low-risk, non-default pathway.
conditions: IF opik outputs are copied into a Pathway pipeline as text instructions
IF Pathway is configured to parse upstream text as commands rather than data
mitigations: Keep opik outputs as structured data only
Disable any text-to-command parsing in Pathway
Insert a validation step that strips instruction-like tokens
Use separate workspaces for generation and processing
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Opik has broad network egress and REST API access, while Pathway is a document-processing agent with no network egress and no file I/O listed. If sensitive documents are routed through opik before Pathway, opik can transmit context off-box by default, creating a leakage path even though Pathway itself is locally constrained. The pairwise risk exists in default opik configurations.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are processed by opik before reaching Pathway
IF opik is allowed to send API payloads containing document contents
mitigations: Route only redacted text into opik
Disable outbound API calls for sensitive jobs
Split sensitive and non-sensitive pipelines
Review opik egress destinations before deployment
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on API payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Opik exposes REST API calls and broad network egress, but Pathway has no filesystem write, no git modification, no shell, and no network egress. There is no overlapping mutable resource or write surface in the profiles, so a direct capability conflict is not plausible from the documented pair.
conditions: IF Pathway is extended with write access to the same mutable resource as opik
IF an external orchestrator grants both agents shared write locks
mitigations: Keep Pathway read-only
Avoid shared mutable directories
Do not grant shared git credentials
Use separate service accounts
requires-engineering: add resource locking if writes are introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: Opik can produce API-driven outputs, and Pathway is a document-processing system that may consume upstream artifacts. If Pathway treats opik output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream documents or analytics. Pathway’s lack of explicit verification controls in the profile makes this a plausible default-integration risk, though not proven severe.
conditions: IF Pathway ingests opik-generated text or metadata without validation
IF downstream consumers rely on Pathway outputs as authoritative
mitigations: Add schema validation before ingestion
Require human review for high-impact outputs
Compare opik outputs against a second source
Log provenance for each record
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no touched data classes, secrets, or residency constraints. The only compliance-relevant difference is opik’s broad network egress versus Pathway’s no-egress profile, which could matter if regulated data is introduced later. With no documented regulated-data flow, this is a low, conditional compliance concern.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into opik before Pathway
IF deployment policy forbids outbound transmission of that data class
mitigations: Classify data before routing
Block regulated data from opik egress
Document retention settings for both systems
Use separate environments for regulated workloads
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
